haiku-low.q1: The breach streak reaches 3 and rule_state has no open incident. The winning evaluator inserts a level-0 incident; a unique index backs this.
haiku-low.q2: The breach count on the open incident goes up by one. No page is sent.
haiku-low.q3: The clear streak reaches 10 with an incident open; status becomes resolved in the same transaction. Each paged person gets one resolved notice. A later breach opens a new incident.
haiku-low.q4: Primary first, then secondary after 5 minutes unanswered, then EM 5 minutes later. Each page tries push, then SMS if push fails or gets no answer in 10 s.
haiku-low.q5: SMS is sent after a push error or 10 s without answer. Every attempt is logged. If both fail, it is logged as failed and escalation still runs.
haiku-low.q6: Each person with a page_log row for the incident gets one resolved notice, push then SMS. No timer is queued; pending escalate timers later do nothing.
haiku-low.q7: In Postgres, rule_state holds the breach and clear streaks per service and rule. A neither minute resets both; a breach resets clear, and a clear minute resets breach.
haiku-low.q8: Each minute, both insert an evaluation row keyed by service, rule and minute; only the successful insert acts, the other stops. Streak and incident changes commit in one transaction.
haiku-low.q9: A 5-minute timer queues an escalate message naming the incident and level. The incident manager locks the row and pages the next level only if open, unacked and still at that level.
haiku-low.q10: The provider calls the webhook with the page reference; page_log maps it to the incident, and the incident manager sets acked time if empty. Escalate then finds it acked and does nothing.
haiku-low.q11: The schedule service is queried at the moment of sending, so a 09:00 handover is respected. If the lookup fails, a failed row with no person is logged.
haiku-low.q12: It reads the person from page_log rows for that incident, not a fresh schedule lookup. Each distinct person with a row gets one notice.

sonnet.q1: The breach streak reaches 3 (three consecutive breach minutes: trailing 5-min window >2% 5xx and >=500 requests) AND rule_state shows no open incident for that service and rule (a unique index allowing one open incident per service and rule backs this up).
sonnet.q2: Each breach adds one to the incident's breach count and sends no page; no new incident is opened.
sonnet.q3: Resolves when the clear streak reaches 10 (10 quiet/clear minutes, each <1% 5xx) with an incident open; status set to resolved in the same transaction, then resolved notices are sent. A later breach opens a new incident with fresh streaks.
sonnet.q4: Primary (level 0) at incident open, secondary (level 1) 5 minutes later if not acked, then EM (level 2) 5 minutes after that. No timer follows the EM page.
sonnet.q5: If push errors or gets no answer in 10 s, SMS is sent; every attempt is logged. If both fail, it is logged as failed, and the escalate timer is still queued and runs. If the schedule lookup fails, a failed row with no person is logged, nothing is sent, and the timer still runs and moves on to the next level.
sonnet.q6: Each distinct person with a page_log row for the incident gets one resolved notice (push then SMS), regardless of attempts; people at levels never reached get nothing. No timer is queued; pending timers that fire later do nothing because the incident is no longer open.
sonnet.q7: In Postgres, in the rule_state table (one row per service and rule). A neither minute resets both streaks; a breach resets the clear streak and a clear minute resets the breach streak.
sonnet.q8: Both try to insert an evaluation row for service, rule and minute; the unique key lets only one insert succeed, and only that winner handles the minute (the other stops). The streak update and incident change commit in one transaction, so each minute counts once. A unique index allowing one open incident per service and rule prevents two open incidents.
sonnet.q9: A message from the timer queue (queued 5 minutes after a page to primary or secondary) naming the incident and the level it was paged at. The incident manager locks the incident row and pages the next level only if the incident is open, not acked, still at that level, and a next level exists; otherwise it does nothing.
sonnet.q10: The engineer taps Acknowledge in the provider app; the provider calls our webhook with the page's provider reference. page_log maps the reference to the incident; the incident manager locks the row and sets acked time if empty. When a queued escalate later runs, it finds the incident acked and does nothing; the row lock orders ack versus escalate.
sonnet.q11: At the moment of sending each page, by looking up the schedule service for that level then (so a 09:00 handover is respected). Resolved notices are the exception: they use the person from page_log, not a fresh lookup.
sonnet.q12: It reads page_log: each distinct person with a page_log row for the incident gets one notice, using the person recorded there instead of a fresh schedule lookup.
